# Review — odyssey-022 (Odyssey 5.1–96), reviewer pass 1

Format per line: **5.N · field · severity · what was wrong · what I did**

## Changes made

1. **5.7–10 · `t`/`l`/`i`/`n` (segmentation) · high** — Units for line 7 (`Ζεῦ πάτερ ἠδ’ ἄλλοι μάκαρες θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες,`) and lines 8–10 (the repeated three-line wish) were drafted as two separate tap-units, cut at the comma after line 7. But conventions.md's segmentation rule allows a comma-cut *only* when a full stop would otherwise run past four lines. Here the next terminal mark (the ano teleia at the end of line 10) is reachable within exactly four lines, so the comma-cut was not permitted — the note's own stated reason ("so the repeated three-line formula … can stand as its own unit") is not a sanctioned exception. I merged the two units into a single 4-line unit (lines 7–10) ending at the real terminal mark, keeping `p`, `v`, `mark: "Athena speaks"`, and reusing the already-published wording for lines 8–10 in both `l` and `i` "as far as the sentence allows" (per packet.md's rule for a partial-line repeat), and rewrote the note accordingly.

2. **5.7 · `i` · medium (house-rendering fidelity)** — The old unit's `i` read "…blessed gods who **live** forever," which is explicitly listed in conventions.md's table (θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες row) as wording to avoid ("the gods who live for ever"). `l` already correctly had "who **are** forever." Fixed to "are forever" in the merged unit's `i` (folded into fix #1 above).

3. **5.1 · `n` · high (grammar)** — Note claimed "ὤρνυθ’ is an **unaugmented** imperfect of ὄρνυμι." The word is printed with ω (ὤρνυθ’ = ὤρνυτο), which is the regular *temporal augment* of an ο-initial verb (ο → ω); the unaugmented Homeric form would be ὄρνυτο. Corrected the note to say the form is augmented, and explained why.

4. **5.3 · `n` · high (fabricated cross-reference)** — Note claimed "κράτος ἐστὶ μέγιστον echoes the phrase already used of Polyphemus's strength among the Cyclopes." This is impossible: parts are drafted in poem order, and Polyphemus does not appear until Book 9, many parts after odyssey-022 (Book 5) — nothing about him could already be "used" at this point in the pipeline. Removed the false claim and replaced it with an accurate gloss of the relative clause itself.

5. **5.28 · `l` · medium (house-rendering fidelity)** — `l` for ἦ ῥα began "**So** he spoke, and…". Conventions.md's table fixes ἦ ῥα as `l`: "He/She spoke", and explicitly lists "So he spoke" in the *avoided* column, reserved for ὣς φάτο / ὣς ἔφατο. Changed to "He spoke, and to Hermes too, his dear son, he spoke face to face:".

6. **5.94 · `n` · high (grammar)** — Note claimed "πῖνε and ἦσθε are **both unaugmented** imperfects." πῖνε (πίνω) is indeed unaugmented, but ἦσθε (ἔδω 'eat') shows the regular augment of an ε-initial verb (ε → η); LSJ/Cunliffe contrast this with the unaugmented 3rd-plural ἔδον found elsewhere in Homer. Corrected the note to separate the two claims correctly.

7. **5.91 · `l`/`i`/`n` · high (quotation marks)** — Calypso's speech (marked "Calypso speaks" at 5.87) is grammatically complete at line 91 ("ἀλλ’ ἕπεο προτέρω, ἵνα τοι πὰρ ξείνια θείω.") — the very next unit opens with the narrator's fixed speech-closing formula ὥς ἄρα φωνήσασα ("So she spoke, and…"). The closing `”` was missing from both `l` and `i` of the 5.91 unit even though the speech is not continued or reopened elsewhere in this part (Hermes's reply, which answers it, belongs to the next part and is a new, separate speech). Added the closing `”` to `l` and `i`, and rewrote the note to explain why the quote closes here rather than after the meal.

8. **5.47 · `n` · medium (notes must not assert unshown poem content)** — Note ended "...a power tied to his later role as guide of the dead," referring to Hermes Psychopompos, a role the poem shows only in Book 24 (the Second Nekyia), far beyond any part drafted so far. This violates conventions.md's Notes rule ("A note asserts nothing about the rest of the poem that this part cannot show"). Trimmed the clause.

9. **5.89–90 · `n` · medium (notes must not assert unshown poem content)** — Note ended "...as indeed proves true," asserting that Calypso does yield to Zeus's order — an outcome that occurs only after this part ends (Hermes hasn't even delivered his message yet within odyssey-022). Trimmed to a hedged, present-tense description of the ambiguity instead.

10. **5.72 · `n` · medium (lemma error)** — Note identified θήλεον as "an unaugmented imperfect of **θάλλω**." LSJ lemmatizes θήλεον under the distinct, root-cognate verb **θηλέω** ('bloom, teem'), not as a form of θάλλω itself (whose own pluperfect-as-imperfect, τεθήλει, appears one line earlier at 5.69 and is correctly identified there). Corrected the lemma and clarified the relationship between the two verbs.

## Findings considered but not acted on

- **5.76 (ἤλυθεν) · `n`** — Note calls ἤλυθεν "an unaugmented aorist of ἔρχομαι on the epic root ἐλυθ-." I am not fully confident this is wrong (unlike the ὤρνυθ’/ἦσθε cases, where the augment rule is unambiguous): Homer's η-forms of this suppletive aorist (ἦλθον/ἤλυθον) are so overwhelmingly the norm in the indicative that some grammarians treat the epic ἐλυθ-/ἠλυθ- alternation itself, rather than a live augment/no-augment choice, as doing the metrical work here. Rather than risk swapping in a wrong claim, I left this note as drafted and flag it here for the second reviewer to check against Monro or Smyth directly.
- **5.66–67 (σκῶπες / κορῶναι εἰνάλιαι) and 5.60 (θύον)** — species/identity genuinely uncertain; already flagged both in the unit notes and in new-renderings.md's own QUESTIONS section by the drafter. No further action needed.
- **5.27 (mid-line ano teleia after νηὶ)** — Already correctly handled: the drafter split the tap-unit at the printed ano teleia (a legitimate terminal mark), and flagged the unusual punctuation for QUESTIONS.md. This is not a segmentation error (contrast with the 5.7–10 case above, where no terminal mark existed at the cut point).
- **5.33–36 (comma-cut ending "τιμήσουσιν,")** — Verified legitimate: the whole clause 5.33–40 has no terminal mark before line 40, so cutting at line 36 (the last comma within the 4-line cap) is exactly the sanctioned exception, unlike the 5.7–10 case.
- **5.90 (τετελεσμένον ἐστίν)** — The drafter's interpretive reading ("ordained/fated" rather than merely "possible") is already flagged as a judgment call in new-renderings.md's QUESTIONS section. I only trimmed the note's overreaching final clause (#9 above); the underlying interpretive choice itself is reasonable and left to the second reviewer.
- **ἐυπλόκαμος "fine-plaited" (5.30, 5.58)** — Used consistently and correctly throughout this part and matches its earlier use at 1.86, but it still has no dedicated row of its own in conventions.md's house-rendering table (only a passing parenthetical mention under the ἐυπλοκαμῖδες row). This is a pre-existing gap in the table, not a defect introduced by this drafter; flagging so the table can be given a proper row at the next conventions update, but not something to fix inside this part's units.json.
- **5.73–74 (i: "even a god… might well stand and marvel at the sight, and take delight in his heart")** — This phrasing sits close in shape to a well-known modern translation's rendering of the same couplet (marvel + delight of heart). On inspection, both elements are direct, almost unavoidable literal renderings of θηήσαιτο and τερφθείη φρεσὶν ᾗσιν, and no distinctive non-literal turn of phrase was borrowed. Left as is, but noting it here in case the second reviewer reads it differently.
- **Diectasis flag density** — Conventions.md asks that Homeric features (including diectasis, e.g. αἰτιόωνται) be flagged on first occurrence in a part. τηλεθόωσα (5.63) is flagged as diectasis; ἠγνοίησεν (5.77) is a milder, arguably-diectasis-adjacent epic lengthening that isn't flagged. Not required (one clear example is already given) — noted but not acted on.

- **House-rendering fidelity**: cross-checked νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς / τέκνον ἐμόν pair, ἕρκος ὀδόντων, διάκτορος ἀργεϊφόντης and ἀργεϊφόντης alone (all 4 occurrences, 5.43/49/75/94), ταλασίφρονος, δῖα θεάων (both occurrences, 5.78/85), ἁλὸς/πόντον ἀτρυγέτοιο (including the documented extension to πόντος at 5.84), πατρίδα γαῖαν (all 4 occurrences with varying possessives), and the sandals formula — all consistent with conventions.md and with each other, apart from the two fixed above.
- **Quotation marks**: all four marked speeches (Athena 5.7, Zeus 5.22, Zeus-to-Hermes 5.29, Calypso 5.87) open with “ in both `l` and `i`; three close correctly within this part (5.20, 5.27, 5.41); Calypso's closes at 5.91 after the fix above. No stray quotation marks elsewhere.
- **New house renderings** (new-renderings.md): all ten new entries plus the μεγαλήτωρ extension were checked against the existing table's method and "avoided on purpose" pattern — all are literal, non-anachronistic, and correctly kept apart from adjacent fixed formulas (e.g. ἰοειδής kept distinct from the other three sea-colour epithets, δάκρυα λείβων kept distinct from δάκρυ χέων). No changes needed; new-renderings.md itself required no edits.
